extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and their representatives filing international (PCT) applications with the European Patent Office (EPO) as receiving Office
extracted.subtask_short: PCT filing at EPO receiving office
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and procedural requirements for filing international (PCT) applications at the European Patent Office as the competent receiving Office, including languages, formats, fees, agent/power-of-attorney rules, and treatment of priority restoration requests. Intended to guide applicants on what the EPO accepts and expects when acting as a PCT receiving Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent receiving Office / for which nationals and residents
rubrics_metrics.description: European Patent Office (EP) is the competent receiving Office for nationals and residents of: Albania, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, San Marino, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, Turkey, United Kingdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages in which international applications may be filed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also states the language(s) in which the Request may be filed: English, French or German.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of paper copies required by the receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 (one) copy on paper required by the receiving Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of PCT‑EASY format
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the receiving Office accept the filing of international applications with requests in PCT‑EASY format? — No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote references EPO notice that it no longer accepts filings in PCT‑EASY format (see OJ EPO 1/2007 and PCT Gazette notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of electronic filing and accepted methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the receiving Office accept the filing of international applications in electronic form? — Yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office accepts XML and PDF files filed using PCT‑SAFE or EPO Online Filing. Offline filings may be furnished on CD‑R. See relevant PCT Gazette and OJ EPO notices for further detail. (Also note fee reductions where international application is filed in electronic form in accordance with Part 7 and Annex F of the Administrative Instructions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of application documents in pre‑conversion format (Administrative Instruction 706)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the Office accept the inclusion of application documents in pre‑conversion format? — Yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files should be in ZIP format and contain texts in ASCII plain text, Microsoft Word 97 (or later), Corel WordPerfect 6.1, 8 and 10 (or later), Writer of OpenOffice 2.0 (or later) (including StarOffice). Where the international application contains a sequence listing as a separate part of the description it should preferably be furnished in compliance with WIPO Standard ST.25 text format; no additional fees are due for sequence listings filed in this format. If sequence listings are filed as image files (e.g. PDF), fees are due for each page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of requests for restoration of right of priority (PCT Rule 26bis.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the receiving Office accept requests for restoration of the right of priority? — Yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office applies the “due care” criterion to such requests (i.e., restoration under PCT Rule 26bis.3 is considered on the basis of whether the failure to file within the priority period occurred despite all due care required by the circumstances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent International Searching Authority (ISA)
rubrics_metrics.description: European Patent Office is the competent International Searching Authority for this receiving Office entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: European Patent Office is the competent International Preliminary Examining Authority for this receiving Office entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees payable to the receiving Office (summary of fee types and amounts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists transmittal fee, international filing fee, fee per sheet in excess of 30, reductions under the Schedule of Fees, electronic filing reductions, search fee, fee for priority document, and fee for requesting restoration of the right of priority (PCT Rule 26bis.3(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As presented on the page: Currency Euro (EUR). Transmittal fee: EUR 125. International filing fee: EUR 1,100. Fee per sheet in excess of 30: EUR 12. Reductions (under Schedule of Fees, item 4) and electronic filing reductions are shown (parenthesised figures apply as from 1 Jan 2014). Search fee: EUR 165 (parenthesis 163 applicable from 1 Jan 2014 noted). Fee for priority document: EUR 248. Fee for requesting restoration of the right of priority (PCT Rule 26bis.3(d)): See Annex D(EP) / EUR 50 (parenthesis 244/163/1,084 figures appear in the table and are footnoted — consult the EPO table/Annex D(EP) for precise current amounts and applicability dates). (Footnotes: amounts in parentheses are applicable as from 1 Jan 2014; see Annex D(EP) for details.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing reductions and character‑coded filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reductions available where request (or request, description, claims and abstract) are filed in character coded format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table indicates reduced amounts (parenthesised) when filed electronically (see Schedule of Fees item 4 and Annex D(EP)); consult the EPO notices and Annex D(EP) for exact reduced amounts and conditions. Also reference to Administrative Instructions Part 7 and Annex F for fee reduction eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must use an agent (is an agent required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is an agent required by the receiving Office? — No, if the applicant has a residence or his principal place of business in one of the States party to the European Patent Convention. Yes, if he has neither a residence nor his principal place of business within the territory of one of those States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can act as agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Any professional representative entered on the relevant list maintained by the EPO; any legal practitioner qualified to practice in patent matters in one of the States party to the European Patent Convention and who has his place of business in that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directory of professional representatives can be ordered at the EPO, Vienna, or consulted on the EPO web site. Where appointing representatives practising within an association registered with the EPO under Rule 152(11) EPC, the association name and registration number should be indicated in Box IV of the Request form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of requirement for a separate power of attorney (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the Office waived the requirement that a separate power of attorney be submitted? — Yes (waiver in general applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particular instances in which a separate power of attorney is required: (1) where a procedural act is performed by a purported agent who is not the agent of record, unless the purported agent belongs to the same office as the agent of record or both the purported agent and the agent of record are employees of the applicant (or, if more than one applicant, of the common representative); (2) in case of doubt as to whether the agent or common representative is entitled to act. Waivers do not apply where the agent or common representative submits any notice of withdrawal during the international phase (see PCT Rule 90bis.1 to 90bis.4 and related rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of requirement for submission of a copy of a general power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the Office waived the requirement that a copy of a general power of attorney be submitted? — Yes (waiver in general applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particular instances in which a copy of a general power of attorney is required are the same as for a separate power of attorney (see above): (1) acts by a purported agent not agent of record, unless they belong to same office or are employees of applicant; (2) doubt as to entitlement to act.
